title: Finite curve modification quotient: finite support, germs and Euler characteristic
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a proper reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension], and let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite surjective $k$-morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Suppose there is an open subset $N\subseteq X$ containing the generic point of every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] such that $f^{-1}(N)\to N$ is an isomorphism. Put $B=f_*\mathcal O_Y$ and $F=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal O_X\to B)$, with direct image and cokernel in the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; thus $B(U)=\mathcal O_Y(f^{-1}U)$ and the cokernel is the sheafification of the sectionwise quotient. Then $\mathcal O_X\to B$ is injective, $B$ and $F$ are coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow0$$
is a short exact sequence. The support $S=\{y\in X:F_y\ne0\}$, where $F_y=\varinjlim_{y\in U}F(U)$, is a finite set of closed points. The $k$-linear germs map is an isomorphism
$$\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\bigoplus_{y\in S}F_y.$$
Every stalk $F_y$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, $H^q(X,F)=0$ for $q>0$ [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and
$$\chi(X,F)=\sum_{y\in S}\dim_k F_y=\sum_{y\in X\text{ closed}}\dim_k F_y$$
[def-pc-euler-characteristic]. The sum over closed points has only finitely many nonzero terms. Neither connectedness nor nodality nor normality of $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), injectivity and finite-support normalization-sequence argument, generalized here to a finite surjective map that is an isomorphism near every component generic point; Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), parts (2)--(4).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] to $X$ and the invertible module $\mathcal O_X$ (trivial rank-one frame). Thus $X$ is Noetherian and $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $B=f_*\mathcal O_Y$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, so [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes $B$ coherent. The canonical structure map is $\mathcal O_X$-linear. Its sheaf cokernel $F$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](1). No reducedness or normality of $Y$ enters this argument.

The finite morphism $f$ is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). Its topological image is all of $X$, hence dense. As $X$ is reduced, [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic] says its scheme-theoretic image is $X$. For a quasi-compact morphism the ideal defining that image is the actual kernel of $\mathcal O_X\to f_*\mathcal O_Y$, by [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Therefore this kernel is zero, proving the required injectivity.

source.place: Tags 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated), 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image) and 056D (lemma-reduced-scheme-theoretically-dense); reduced dense-image criterion as in the current blueprint lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic.

proof.text: In the abelian category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the cokernel projection $B\to F$ is epic and its kernel is the image of $\mathcal O_X\to B$. Together with Step 2 this is precisely the short exact sequence in [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Over $N$ the given scheme isomorphism identifies the structure map with the identity of $\mathcal O_N$. Hence the cokernel is zero on $N$: locally every section of $B$ is in the image there, so its class in the sheafified quotient is zero. Thus $S\subseteq E:=X\setminus N$.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), proof of the normalization short exact sequence, applied to the stated isomorphism locus N.

proof.text: Every point $x$ of $E$ is closed in $X$. Indeed the Noetherian closed-subset component theorem [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], applied first to $X$, puts $x$ in an irreducible component $C$ of dimension one. It is not the generic point of $C$, since that point lies in $N$. Thus $\overline{\{x\}}\subsetneq C$. If $y\ne x$ were a specialization of $x$, sobriety and its uniqueness clause [lem-sc-scheme-sober] give $\overline{\{y\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{x\}}\subsetneq C$, contradicting dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Apply the same Noetherian closed-subset component theorem to the closed subset $E$. Each of its finitely many irreducible components has a generic point by sobriety, and that point is closed in $X$ by the preceding argument; hence each component is a singleton. Therefore $E$, and thus $S\subseteq E$, is finite and consists of closed points. In particular $S$ is closed and has dimension at most zero; the empty case is included.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), proof: the non-isomorphism locus in a Noetherian curve is discrete closed; properties.tex Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components), schemes.tex Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coherent-finite-support-skyscrapers] using Step 1 and Step 4. It gives the canonical module-sheaf isomorphism $F\simeq\bigoplus_{y\in S}\mathscr S_y(F_y)$ whose components send sections to germs. Evaluate it on $X$. Since $S$ is finite, the sum is also the finite product, and its sections are componentwise tuples; by the explicit skyscraper sections each summand contributes exactly $F_y$. Thus the resulting isomorphism is exactly the displayed germs map $\Gamma(X,F)\to\bigoplus_{y\in S}F_y$. The scalar action in that node is through structure-sheaf germs, so the map is $k$-linear.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), part (2); Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), finite closed-support skyscraper description.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-coherent-zero-dimensional-support], applied to the coherent module $F$ on the locally Noetherian scheme $X$ with the zero-dimensional support of Step 4, $H^q(X,F)=0$ for all $q>0$. Apply [lem-pc-coherent-hi] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: the field $k$ is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $k$), so $H^0(X,F)$ is a finite $k$-module. The degree-zero comparison [lem-sc-open-cohomology-zero-sections], with $U=X$, identifies it with $\Gamma(X,F)$. Hence this section space is finite-dimensional. Step 5 identifies every $F_y$ for $y\in S$ with a direct summand of that finite-dimensional vector space, so each has finite dimension. For $y\notin S$, $F_y=0$ by the definition of $S$, which covers every other stalk.

By [def-pc-euler-characteristic] and Step 6, all positive-degree terms in the Euler sum vanish, so $\chi(X,F)=\dim_k\Gamma(X,F)$. The dimension of the finite direct sum in Step 5 is the sum of the dimensions of its summands: concatenate finite bases of the $F_y$. This gives $\chi(X,F)=\sum_{y\in S}\dim_kF_y$. Every closed point outside $S$ has zero stalk, so extending this finite sum to all closed points adds only zero terms. If $S$ is empty, Step 5 gives the zero section space and every asserted sum is zero.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), parts (2)--(4), and the finite-dimensional direct-sum dimension formula.

The item statement is byte-identical to live (unsplit). The only change outside the proof is the stmt_dep def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence, which is correct because the statement asserts a short exact sequence. No new nodes, no repair note, no SGA citation. Step 1: the proper-field lemma with O_X makes X Noetherian; the finite-morphism def gives B quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent (01XZ node); the coherent cokernel node makes F coherent. Step 2: finite implies affine, hence qcqs (affine-permanence (3)), surjective gives dense image, and X reduced gives SIm=X by the reduced-dense-image lemma; the schematic-image def says the kernel ideal is the actual kernel for quasi-compact maps, so O_X→B is injective. Step 3 (elementary): the sequence comes from the abelian cokernel, F|_N=0, so S⊆X∖N. Step 4: each x∉N is closed, because a specialization y≠x would give cl{y}⊊cl{x}⊊C (sober uniqueness), contradicting pure dimension 1; the components of the closed set E are therefore closed points, so E is finite. Step 5: the finite-support skyscraper node, evaluated at X, gives the k-linear germs isomorphism. Step 6: zero-dimensional support gives H^q=0 for q>0 (Zariski convention), 02O6 over Spec k gives H^0 finite, and H^0=Γ; stalks are summands of Γ, so finite-dimensional. Step 7: χ=dim Γ=Σ dim F_y. Edge cases checked: f an isomorphism, the nodal cubic (defect 1), a node with a degree-2 residue field, nonreduced Y with an embedded thickening, and empty X. Duplicate search (0C1R, delta-invariant, normalization sequence): existing nodes all need k algebraically closed, the normalization or nodality, so none duplicates the item. I accept all ten off-unit generic tool_uses.

lean.statement: theorem finite_curve_quotient_stalk_euler (k : Type u) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsReduced X] (hdim : X.IsPureDimension 1) (f : Y ⟶ X) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] [IsFinite f] [Surjective f] (N : X.Opens) (hN : ∀ (Z : Set X), Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X → ∀ x : X, IsGenericPoint x Z → x ∈ N) (hiso : IsIso (morphismRestrict f N)) : Mono (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit f.toRingCatSheafHom) ∧ RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace ((pushforward f).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf)) ∧ RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (finiteCurveQuotient f) ∧ (ShortComplex.mk (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit f.toRingCatSheafHom) (cokernel.π (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit f.toRingCatSheafHom)) (cokernel.condition _)).ShortExact ∧ (∀ x : X, FiniteDimensional k (finiteCurveQuotientStalk k f x)) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace q).obj (finiteCurveQuotient f))) ∧ ∃ S : Finset X, (∀ x : X, x ∈ S ↔ ¬ Subsingleton ((finiteCurveQuotient f).presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ (∀ x ∈ S, IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) ∧ (∃ e : finiteCurveQuotientSections k f ≃ₗ[k] ⨁ x : {x : X // x ∈ S}, finiteCurveQuotientStalk k f x.val, ∀ (s : finiteCurveQuotientSections k f) (x : {x : X // x ∈ S}), e s x = (finiteCurveQuotient f).presheaf.germ ⊤ x.val (Set.mem_univ x.val) s) ∧ (finiteCurveQuotient f).eulerChar k = ∑ x ∈ S, (Module.finrank k (finiteCurveQuotientStalk k f x) : ℤ) ∧ (finiteCurveQuotient f).eulerChar k = ∑ᶠ x : {x : X // IsClosed ({x} : Set X)}, (Module.finrank k (finiteCurveQuotientStalk k f x.val) : ℤ) ∧ (Set.Finite {x : {x : X // IsClosed ({x} : Set X)} | (Module.finrank k (finiteCurveQuotientStalk k f x.val) : ℤ) ≠ 0})
